m8-t1.introduction: A second way to understand “Build a credible HR analytics portfolio”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: A portfolio is an honest decision story
sections.explanation: Explain the question, population, evidence, method, recommendation and limits so another person can inspect your judgement.

items.label: Question and population
items.detail: Define what the analysis was meant to support.

items.label: Data and method
items.detail: Show sources, cleaning, formulas and checks.

items.label: Finding and limitation
items.detail: Explain what is supported and what remains uncertain.

items.label: Recommendation
items.detail: State a proportionate next step with an owner.

sections.takeaway: Label simulations as classroom work and do not invent paid clients, employer experience or business savings.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A reviewer should be able to reproduce the headline
sections.explanation: An evidence index is useful only when sources, transformations and final versions remain aligned.

items.label: Preserve inputs
items.detail: Retain raw synthetic data and a dictionary.

items.label: Record transformations
items.detail: Keep the cleaning log and formula or pivot notes.

items.label: Run QA
items.detail: Reproduce headline values and check filters.

items.label: Align versions
items.detail: Keep the memo, dashboard and evidence index consistent.

sections.takeaway: Keep editable working evidence in the approved submission area and publish only safe aggregates.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Match the evidence to the job’s actual tasks
sections.explanation: Different entry-level HR roles emphasise different work. Titles vary, so use the real job description.

items.label: HR Executive
items.detail: Show accurate records, coordination and responsible handling.

items.label: HR Analyst
items.detail: Show definitions, reproducibility and cautious interpretation.

items.label: Talent Acquisition
items.detail: Show matched funnels, communication and structured selection support.

sections.takeaway: Distinguish your contribution from team work and avoid claiming authority the course did not confer.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Can you present the Namma People Services practice analysis as paid consulting experience?
checkpoint.answer: No. It is legitimate portfolio evidence when labelled as synthetic classroom work with your actual contribution and limitations.

m8-t2.introduction: A second way to understand “HR interviews and stakeholder conversations”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Clarify the definition before the arithmetic
sections.explanation: An ambiguous metric question needs a population, period, unit and denominator before a meaningful number can be calculated.

items.label: Clarify the question
items.detail: Name the decision and the requested metric.

items.label: Set the boundary
items.detail: Confirm period, population and counting rules.

items.label: Show the calculation
items.detail: Use a small reproducible example with units.

items.label: Explain limits
items.detail: State assumptions and what must be verified.

sections.takeaway: If an employer’s convention is unknown, say so and ask for its dictionary.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Use STAR without inventing a past event
sections.explanation: A course artefact can demonstrate a real decision or correction if its simulated setting is clear.

items.label: Situation and task
items.detail: Give the honest context and your responsibility.

items.label: Action
items.detail: Explain your own method and correction.

items.label: Result
items.detail: State only outcomes supported by the practice evidence.

items.label: Learning
items.detail: Describe how the experience changed your checking habit.

sections.takeaway: For a hypothetical question, describe what you would do rather than claiming it already happened.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Urgency does not grant raw-data access
sections.explanation: An analyst can support a request while preserving the institution’s access and escalation boundaries.

items.label: Confirm purpose
items.detail: Ask what the requester needs to decide.

items.label: Check recipient authority
items.detail: Verify actual access rather than relying on urgency.

items.label: Minimise the response
items.detail: Use a safe aggregate when it answers the question.

items.label: Escalate the decision
items.detail: Identify the appropriate qualified owner when the request exceeds your role.

sections.takeaway: Escalate legal, health, discrimination and employment decisions to qualified authorised roles.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: A manager says a raw employee export is urgent. Does that alone authorise sharing it?
checkpoint.answer: No. Confirm purpose, recipient access and the minimum necessary layer, then follow the institution’s approved sharing or escalation process.

m8-t3.introduction: A second way to understand “Capstone presentation and analytical development”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Present the decision path, not a software tour
sections.explanation: A clear presentation connects the question to evidence and a proportionate action. The dashboard is supporting material, not the argument itself.

items.label: Question and audience
items.detail: Name the decision and authorised viewer.

items.label: Data and checks
items.detail: Explain sources, definitions, quality and safeguards.

items.label: Findings and limits
items.detail: Show a few truthful visuals with uncertainty.

items.label: Action and evaluation
items.detail: Name the owner, test and review trigger.

sections.takeaway: Do not imply an external professional or software-vendor credential from this course’s completion.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A correction should propagate to dependent claims
sections.explanation: When an error is found, identify what uses that value rather than changing a single visible number.

items.label: Reproduce the issue
items.detail: Find the faulty input, formula or definition.

items.label: Trace dependencies
items.detail: Identify affected rates, charts and conclusions.

items.label: Correct and retest
items.detail: Recalculate and rerun the relevant QA.

items.label: Update the recommendation
items.detail: Revise the memo and evidence index consistently.

sections.takeaway: A transparent correction is stronger analytical practice than defending a result you know is wrong.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Build the next skill through a bounded practice task
sections.explanation: A development plan should name a useful task, evidence, reviewer and date linked to the target role.

items.label: Choose a role skill
items.detail: Pick a specific gap such as joins, cohort tracking or filter QA.

items.label: Define a practice case
items.detail: Use synthetic or explicitly authorised material.

items.label: Arrange review
items.detail: Name an appropriate reviewer and date.

items.label: Keep evidence of progress
items.detail: Store the correction, result and next learning question.

sections.takeaway: Seek supervised authorised practice; do not collect real employee records independently for a portfolio.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: If the jury finds a wrong denominator, is changing only the dashboard label enough?
checkpoint.answer: No. Trace every dependent rate, chart and recommendation, correct the calculation, retest it and update the aligned evidence and memo.

sections.title: Responsible recruitment and workforce insight: connect the question to evidence
sections.explanation: An integrated, reproducible synthetic portfolio connecting data quality, recruitment, workforce capacity and a bounded authorised recommendation.

items.label: Question
items.detail: An integrated, reproducible synthetic portfolio connecting data quality, recruitment, workforce capacity and a bounded authorised recommendation.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Use the original practice material with explicit provenance.

items.label: Decision
items.detail: Explain a bounded recommendation and the evidence that could change it.

sections.takeaway: The app records reading and quizzes; external project submission, verification and marking remain with the institution.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Keep synthetic fixtures and authority boundaries separate
sections.explanation: The practice tables are independent examples, not linked real employee records. Use the original inputs and log every deliberate scenario change.

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Identify the fixture, grain, period and original source copy.

items.label: Separation
items.detail: Do not join independent populations as if they were one company dataset.

items.label: Permission
items.detail: Use synthetic inputs and the institution-approved submission route.

items.label: Honest context
items.detail: Do not report simulated interviews, approvals or outcomes as live events.

sections.takeaway: No real personal dataset, paid tool or live organisational access is required or authorised by this project.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Reserve time for correction, not only construction
sections.explanation: The original work-plan table supplies the timing. This map groups the work into a review loop without changing those allocations.

items.label: Frame
items.detail: Read the decision and inspect source boundaries.

items.label: Build
items.detail: Create the required artefacts with traceable formulas or decisions.

items.label: Check
items.detail: Reproduce the headline and inspect assumptions and safeguards.

items.label: Review and revise
items.detail: Use peer or self-review and keep a change log.

items.label: Explain and submit
items.detail: Finish the recommendation, disclosure and evidence index.

sections.takeaway: A first draft is not a finished artefact; retain the comment and your response after review.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Organise the responsible recruitment and workforce insight submission
sections.explanation: These groups help you locate evidence; the full numbered submission checklist above still defines every required component.

items.label: Decision and source package
items.detail: Keep the brief, source inventory, dictionary, raw data and cleaning log.

items.label: Reconciled analyses
items.detail: Show exact populations, formulas and independent checks.

items.label: Safe dashboard
items.detail: Include accessible charts, filter QA and disclosure review.

items.label: Decision memo
items.detail: Compare options with an owner, uncertainty and a balancing measure.

items.label: Responsible-analytics review
items.detail: Discuss causal limits, model claims, fairness signals and accountability.

items.label: Individual defence
items.detail: Provide the five-minute presentation and original contribution/reflection requirements.

sections.takeaway: A public portfolio copy must be safe and clearly labelled; it is not a substitute for the editable institutional submission.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Let evidence and safeguards constrain the capstone
sections.explanation: An integrated portfolio is credible when the sources, calculations, sharing choices and recommendation can all withstand an individual defence.

items.label: Declare the inputs
items.detail: Use synthetic fixtures and preserve their separate populations and periods.

items.label: Reproduce the headline
items.detail: Show definitions, transformations and independently checked calculations.

items.label: Share safely
items.detail: Use aggregate accessible views with filter and indirect-disclosure QA.

items.label: Bound the recommendation
items.detail: State uncertainty, an authorised owner, an evaluation plan and your actual contribution.

sections.takeaway: Do not infer demographic attributes, create individual leaver-risk lists or automate employment decisions. The project does not confer an external HR or software-vendor certification.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Follow the original rubric and its evidence standard
sections.explanation: The original block or capstone marks, performance anchors and institutional award conditions are unchanged.

items.label: Problem and scope
items.detail: Define the decision, population and permitted use clearly.

items.label: Technical reproducibility
items.detail: Provide checked calculations, definitions and an inspectable method.

items.label: Judgement and safeguards
items.detail: Let privacy, fairness and causal limitations constrain claims.

items.label: Decision quality
items.detail: Recommend a practical, proportionate and reviewable action.

items.label: Presentation and defence
items.detail: Explain your contribution and reproduce key evidence.

sections.takeaway: These panels and animations do not calculate marks, approve projects or award an external credential.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Review the recommendation from a challenger’s view
sections.explanation: A reviewer should be able to trace a claim, test an assumption and understand which action needs another role’s approval.

items.label: Trace a headline
items.detail: Find the calculation or artefact behind the main claim.

items.label: Challenge an assumption
items.detail: Ask what missing evidence could reverse the action.

items.label: Check authority
items.detail: Name who is permitted to approve a consequential decision.

items.label: Inspect sharing
items.detail: Choose evidence that can safely appear in the public version.

sections.takeaway: Keep the actual review comment and your correction or explanation instead of claiming a review that never happened.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Explain assistance without outsourcing judgement
sections.explanation: Complete the original AI-use statement even when no AI was used. Tool help must not fabricate records, sources or experience.

items.label: Name tools or none
items.detail: State the actual assistance and permitted synthetic inputs.

items.label: Record your checks
items.detail: Explain accepted, changed and rejected suggestions and independent verification.

items.label: Own the work
items.detail: Describe your contribution, judgement and responsibility for the final claims.

sections.takeaway: Do not upload real employee, candidate, student or credential data to public AI tools; follow exam restrictions separately.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: An extension tests an assumption after the core is complete
sections.explanation: The optional extension is not required for full marks. Keep the original work and distinguish a changed scenario from an observation.

items.label: Complete the core
items.detail: Finish the required evidence and safeguards first.

items.label: A phased evaluation
items.detail: Define the comparison and assumptions needed for a causal interpretation.

items.label: Compare and document
items.detail: Show what changed, which conclusion depends on it and what remains unknown.

checkpoint.question: Would a high aggregate accuracy score authorise an individual employee leaver-risk list in this capstone?
checkpoint.answer: No. Individual leaver-risk lists, real employee or candidate data, inferred demographic attributes and automated employment decisions are prohibited in this project. Use synthetic aggregate literacy and a proportionate, human-accountable recommendation.
